subject: ventures/house-cleaning-quote-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a residential cleaning business with a few two-person crews who prices recurring clients. They would check first that the cost per visit counts every paid person-hour (on-site and paid drive time per cleaner, with payroll burden), that the price floor and margin algebra are right after the card fee, that the 'what list price do I need' answer is the number they actually type into their quote, how add-ons and first/deep cleans are treated on recurring clients, and whether overhead and owner pay are inside or outside the 'margin'

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the shipped sample job (1,800 sq ft, 2 baths, 450 sq ft/person-hour, crew 2, $18 + 12% burden, 15 min drive each way, 14 mi at $0.60, 3% fee, 30% target, $190 list, oven + fridge add-ons) in an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/98bb4f26-7393-5019-a94a-3eb571cb7a13/scratchpad/house-cleaning/hand.py) from the page's stated method and the margin identity P - fP - C = mP: all four lines agree to the cent with analyze() (cost 203.88/126.26/137.35/159.53, floor 304.30/188.45/205.00/238.10, max discount 0/24.62/18.00/4.76%, annual profit 38.62/3522.27/1977.25/850.16, sum 6,388.30, needed list 304.30), and at each floor profit/price equals the target exactly. Drive time counted per riding cleaner matches FLSA 29 CFR 785.38 (travel between job sites is hours worked). But the verdict's instruction is wrong whenever add-ons are listed, as in the shipped example: it says 'list a one-time clean at $304.30 or more', while that figure already includes the $60 of add-on prices; typing $304.30 into 'Your list price for a one-time clean' gives a $364.30 list (one-time margin 41% vs 30% target, weekly 53.7%) and the verdict then reads 'clears ... at a $364.30 list price'. The right entry is $244.30 (verified: margin exactly 30.00%). Core arithmetic is right; the one actionable number is mislabelled, so not 3.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page feature by running calc.mjs: cost per visit, price floor, max discount per frequency, list price needed, annual profit by frequency, add-ons, CSV export (5 rows, matches table), header-optional parsing with tabs and $, quoted '$1,200', validation messages, usage counters with opt-out. All work. Gaps: JSON-LD featureList advertises 'profit per labor hour' but profitPerPersonHour is computed and never shown on the page or in the CSV; the Clear button empties only the two textareas, not the 14 job fields; analyze() with an empty frequency list returns neededListPrice -Infinity and 'Every frequency clears' (the page guards it via parseFrequencies, so not reachable from the UI).
evidence.verification: cd ventures/house-cleaning-quote-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 28 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail. 7 seeded mutants with quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (floor without the fee, add-on supplies dropped, time multiplier dropped, bathroom minutes /30), 3 survived (removing the max-discount clamp at 0, accepting a 100% discount, profitPerPersonHour without drive hours). The add-on/list-price defect above is not covered: the tests assert the verdict only as /1 of 2/ and never combine add-ons with the needed-list instruction. Tests are the author's hand examples; none recompute the sample from an outside source.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (177 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html inline script, usage.mjs. One pure module shared by page and tests, no dependencies, careful splitCells (quoted thousands, tabs, doubled quotes) with a dated comment, inputs validated with named fields, esc() on all injected text. Defects: profitPerPersonHour is dead output; an empty frequency list yields -Infinity and a false 'every frequency clears' verdict instead of an error; a first data line whose visits cell is non-numeric and contains 'visit' or 'frequency' (e.g. 'Weekly visit,fifty-two') is silently taken as a header with no warning; a blank time multiplier silently becomes 1.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'Nothing is uploaded' (page.test asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon; inline script imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs: pass); disclaimer 'No warranty ... not legal, tax, payroll or financial advice' on page and README (pass); 'Not modelled' and 'Unverified' lists on page (pass); 'How it is calculated' formula text matches calc.mjs line for line (pass). Fails: README and page promise 'the list price that makes every discount still clear target', and the verdict states it as a one-time price while it includes add-on prices (wrong whenever add-ons are used); featureList 'profit per labor hour' is not shown anywhere. 'Annual profit' excludes overhead and owner pay; the not-modelled list names insurance and acquisition cost but not admin, software or owner salary. llms.txt points at the old github.io host: source-only (the Pages build rewrites it), not filed.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an owner types a home, their timed sq ft/person-hour, wage, burden, drive and mileage, and their frequency discounts, and gets per-frequency floors and discount limits in seconds; without add-ons the answer is right and directly usable for a recurring quote (sample without add-ons: 'list a one-time clean at $262.21', correct). With add-ons they must notice the list-price label problem. Add-ons apply to every visit of every frequency (the sample sells an inside-oven clean 52 times a year to the weekly client), so a one-off first-visit add-on cannot be modelled. Nearest tools: Jobber/Housecall Pro quote builders and spreadsheet templates price by sq ft or hour but do not show a discount floor per frequency; this does, privately.
evidence.domain: Against standard job costing for residential cleaning (labor person-hours x loaded wage + supplies + vehicle, price = cost / (1 - fee - margin)) and FLSA 29 CFR 785.38 for between-job travel: the cost build-up and algebra are right. Departures a senior owner would raise: the 'target margin' is a contribution margin with no overhead or owner-pay line, while owners usually price to cover overhead (office, software, insurance, owner salary) on top of field labor; add-on minutes are scaled by the frequency's time multiplier (an oven clean takes 45 min on the 1.5x deep clean, 24 min weekly), which is not how add-on time behaves; add-ons recur on every visit; the payment fee is a flat percent with no per-transaction fixed part (2.9% + $0.30 is $6.10 vs $6.00 at $200, immaterial). Documented in 'How it is calculated', but a practitioner would not sign off on the overhead omission without an explicit overhead input.

defects.what: The verdict tells the owner to 'list a one-time clean at $X', but X is neededListPrice, which includes the add-on prices; the page's one-time price field excludes them. On the shipped sample it says $304.30; typing that gives a $364.30 list (margin 41% vs 30% target); the right entry is $244.30. The 'List price so every frequency clears target' tile has the same ambiguity
No overhead or owner-pay input: the 'target margin' and 'Annual profit' are contribution before office, software, insurance and owner salary, and the page does not say the margin must cover them

Add-ons apply to every visit of every frequency and their minutes are scaled by the frequency's time multiplier (oven 45 min on the 1.5x deep clean, 24 min weekly), so a one-off first-visit add-on cannot be modelled and add-on time is distorted
No test combines add-ons with the needed-list verdict, and the max-discount clamp, the 100% discount bound and profitPerPersonHour can be changed with all 28 tests green
JSON-LD featureList advertises 'profit per labor hour' but profitPerPersonHour is never shown on the page or exported in the CSV

A first frequency line with a non-numeric visits cell containing 'visit' or 'frequency' is silently treated as a header (no skipped-line warning); a blank time multiplier silently becomes 1; analyze() with no frequency lines returns -Infinity and 'Every frequency clears'

verdict: A small, honest cost-plus quote calculator whose arithmetic is right: an independent recompute of the shipped sample matches every cost, floor, max discount and annual profit to the cent, the margin algebra holds after the card fee, and drive time is counted per cleaner as FLSA travel rules require. It does not meet the bar because its one actionable instruction is mislabelled: whenever add-ons are listed (as in its own example) the verdict tells the owner to list the one-time clean at a figure that already includes add-on prices, so following it overprices by the add-on total ($304.30 typed gives a $364.30 list; $244.30 is right). A senior owner-operator would also ask where overhead and owner pay go and would not sell an oven clean on every weekly visit. Tests pass (28/28) and catch 4 of 7 seeded mutants; the add-on verdict path is untested.
